title: Contractor onboard sprint (lite) — 45-day retro playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, repeatable onboarding sprint (45 days) tailored for short-to-medium term contractors and project hires. The goal is to get contributors to productive parity for scoped projects while preserving people-ops bandwidth. Use this when the role duration is <= 6 months or when leadership requests a fast ramp.

Scope and assumptions:
- Intended for individual contributors (engineer, data, design contractors) and project PMs.
- Not for executive-level contractors or embedded long-term contractors (>6 months) — they get the full 90-day program.
- Expectation: owner (hiring manager) shares project brief and acceptance criteria day 0.
- We prioritize deliverable-focused onboarding over broad org immersion.

Success criteria (how we measure "onboarded"):
- Contributor delivers first project milestone (PR, design spike, data schema) within 30 days.
- Manager rates contributor >= 3/5 on the quick ramp rubric at day 30 and >= 4/5 at day 45.
- Contractor self-reports confidence >= 3/5 on role clarity at day 14 survey.

Owner and key roles:
- Program owner: Priya Menon (people-ops) — orchestration, templates, alerts
- Hiring manager: (role-specific) — provides project brief, priorities, 1:1s
- Buddy: peer contributor (same discipline) — daily quick sync first 10 days
- Tech ops: provisioning, access, environment setup

Preboarding checklist (to complete before contractor's first day):
- Offer accepted -> create contractor profile and start I-9/contract paperwork
- Create seat in HR system, access to payroll/invoice flow
- Manager adds project brief + acceptance criteria to shared drive
- Tech ops: dev environment, repo access, cloud account, VPN and KMS access if needed
- Admin: calendar invite for day-0 orientation (30 min), buddy intro, and project kickoff
- Microlearning: assign 3 bite-sized modules from training catalog (max 2 hours total)

Day 0 (orientation, 30–60 minutes):
- Quick welcome (people-ops): one-slide role overview, who to ask
- Manager: 15-minute project brief + top 3 priorities for first 30 days
- Buddy: 15-minute walkthrough of the repo, build steps, and dev checklist
- Housekeeping: ticketing tool, Slack channels, calendar norms, expense/invoice flow

Week 1 (days 1–7): focus on momentum
- Daily quick sync (15 min) with buddy for first 7 working days
- Manager check-in at day 3 and end-of-week 1 (15–30 min) to unblock blockers
- Deliverable: setup PR, initial spike, or design draft depending on role
- Microlearning: complete assigned modules, mark "done" in sheet
- People-ops: day-7 pulse survey (single question + free text)

Weeks 2–4: ownership and integration
- 1:1 cadence: manager weekly, buddy twice weekly optional
- Deliverable: first milestone due by day 20–25 (scope set by manager)
- Ops: ensure all access is stable (no escalations >48h)
- People-ops: passive monitoring of survey flags and usage of learning modules

Days 30 and 45 checkpoints (formal rubrics & retro):
- Day 30: manager uses quick ramp rubric (see rubric anchors below). People-ops will collect and store scores. If score <3, manager + people-ops run a remediation plan (10-day bite).
- Day 45: formal 45-day retro with manager, buddy, and contractor. Retro template below — add notes to the contractor file and to the "contractor-healthboard" sheet.

45-day retro template (guide for manager):
- Start: what went well? (3 bullets)
- Stop: blockers or process issues (3 bullets)
- Continue: what should we keep? (2 bullets)
- Impact: demonstrate what the contractor delivered vs expected (attach PR/artefact link)
- Career/engagement: rate the contractor's engagement and recommended next steps (extend, finish, convert)
- Admin: final invoice timing, knowledge handoff checklist, repo cleanup

Quick ramp rubric (manager scoring anchors) — use 1–5 scale
- 5: Exceeds expectations — delivers ahead of schedule, high code/PR quality, independent
- 4: Solid — meets expectations, occasional guidance, dependable
- 3: Developing — completing tasks with clear supervision, learning curve present
- 2: At-risk — missing key deliverables, needs frequent oversight
- 1: Misaligned — role mismatch or serious performance concerns

Interview rubric notes (when hiring contractors) — lightweight panel (30–45 mins)
- Panel composition: hiring manager + 1 peer (same discipline) + people-ops representative (optional for onboarding Qs)
- Timebox: 10 min intro + 25–30 min focused assessment + 5 min score
- Areas to assess: role-relevant skills (60%), problem decomposition (20%), communication and team fit (20%)
- Scorecard anchors: technical sample + 2 scenario questions. Avoid long algorithm-heavy questions for short-contract roles.

Sample contractor-focused questions (pick 3):
- Describe a recent project you delivered in 4–6 weeks. What was the outcome and tradeoffs?
- Given this repo and ticket, how would you approach the spike needed in week 1? (practical plan)
- Tell us about a time you hit a blocker in a short project. How did you escalate and resolve it?

Onboarding handoff checklist (end of engagement or extension):
- Deliver final artifacts, README, and tidy up open PRs or tickets
- Create handoff doc (summary, next steps, known gaps) in project folder
- Transfer credentials/ownership or rotate keys if contractor had privileged access
- Final retro + admin signoff (invoices, contractor offboard tasks)

Microlearning library (recommended modules for contractors, pick 3):
- Project orientation: codebase primer (20–30 min)
- Security quickstart: secrets, KMS basics (15 min)
- Deploy checklist: CI/CD runbook (20 min)
- Communication norms: Slack & async expectations (10 min)

Notes to people-ops (operational reminders):
- Keep the 45-day sheet as the canonical record for short-term hires. Column headers: name, role, manager, start, day7 flag, day30 score, day45 score, outcome.
- Use HR-REQ-4123 as the template for contractor offers and standard SOW language.
- For contractors converting to FT: require a 30-day conversion freeze after conversion decision (org policy).

Open questions / decisions to make (TODOs):
- Should we require a people-ops rep on all contractor interviews under $X budget? (cost threshold)
- Auto-assign buddies or let managers nominate? Pilot auto-assign for Q2 hires.
- Define the "conversion freeze" language in the SOW template — legal check pending.
